IsShared.rationale: multiplayer-only. EventModel.IsShared (EventModel.cs:80-85) has exactly three readers and all are multiplayer: the vote-vs-independent choice split in EventSynchronizer, the shared-event label (NEventLayout.cs:227, gated on `Players.Count > 1`), and the per-event Rng seed term `IsShared ? 0 : GetPlayerSlotIndex(Owner)` (EventModel.cs:238), which is 0 in single player either way -- rng.make_event_rng records exactly that reduction (rng.py:74-80). The fourth use is an assertion that only a shared event may call EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent (EventModel.cs:610-613). Out of scope per the shared contract's multiplayer waiver.

IsAllowed.maps_to: PunchOff.is_allowed (events/punch_off.py:55-57) `run.total_floor >= 6`, matching PunchOff.cs:41-44's `runState.TotalFloor >= 6`. events/punch_off.py:15 names the literal _MIN_FLOOR = 6. No multiplayer quantifier.

AfterEventStarted.rationale: presentation only: PunchOff.cs:55-61 subscribes to RunManager's RoomExited and kicks off PunchEachOther (PunchOff.cs:63-99), an infinite anim/VFX/SFX loop -- TriggerAnim, PlayOnCreatureCenter, NHitSparkVfx, Cmd.Wait, a node Scale flip -- cancelled by a CancellationTokenSource on room exit (PunchOff.cs:138-142) or by TakeThem (PunchOff.cs:121). It deals no damage, applies no power and takes no stream draw; the two Creatures it animates are the display-only ones EV-12 covers.

CalculateVars.maps_to: PunchOff.calculate_vars (events/punch_off.py:59-61) `self.rng.randint(91, 98)`, matching PunchOff.cs:101-104's `DynamicVars.Gold.BaseValue = base.Rng.NextInt(91, 99)`. The bound conversion is right -- NextInt's upper bound is exclusive, so [91, 99) is randint(91, 98), 8 outcomes either way -- and the sim keeps the throwaway draw with a comment saying the GoldVar is never granted by either option (which is true: grep of PunchOff.cs shows no GainGold). One draw in both. Only the stream diverges (EV-3).

guards.maps_to: no sim constant is needed: the var's only job is to declare the DynamicVar slot CalculateVars then overwrites, and neither Nab nor Fight reads DynamicVars.Gold. events/punch_off.py:59-61 rolls it and discards it, which is the same observable.

guards.what: EV-12: a Combat-layout event builds its encounter -- monsters, HP rolls and AfterAddedToRoom -- when the ROOM IS ENTERED, not when the fight starts. EventRoom.EnterInternal calls GenerateInternalCombatState (EventRoom.cs:67-71), which runs `_mutableEncounter.GenerateMonstersWithSlots(runState)` and then CreateCreature + AddCreature per monster (EventModel.cs:383-403); CreateCreature rolls the monster's max HP on RunState.Rng.Niche (CombatState.cs:232-247). EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent then REUSES that state -- `ShouldCreateCombat = (LayoutType != EventLayoutType.Combat)` (EventModel.cs:624-628)
guards.issue: The sim has no room-entry encounter generation at all: events/punch_off.py:77-83 merely records pending_encounter, and run.create_combat (run.py:1135-1152) builds the monsters when the DRIVER runs the fight. Two observables: (1) the draws move -- the game burns them unconditionally at entry, so a player who takes NAB still consumes them, while the sim consumes them only on the FIGHT path; (2) even on the FIGHT path they land at a different point in each stream. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes_a.py combatlayout`): a parity run entering Punch-Off consumes 0 Niche draws on BOTH paths where the game consumes 2, plus 2 encounter-Rng NextInt(2,10) draws. LIVE for parity -- Punch-Off is an ordinary Underdocks event gated only on TotalFloor >= 6, and a desynced Niche/encounter stream misprices every later monster HP roll. MECHANISM EV-12, one verdict at every site (rule 3). Radius: `py audit/tools/event_probes_a.py combatlayout` lists the Combat-layout events in the source -- PunchOff.cs:33, TheLanternKey.cs:15 and TheArchitect.cs:52 (TheArchitect is unported and has no sim unit). event/the_lantern_key is in the radius and is not this record's to verdict.

guards.what: PunchConstruct.StartingHpReduction is applied to the wrong HP value and in the wrong lifecycle slot. PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:15-19 rolls `StartingHpReduction = base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` per construct, and PunchConstruct.AfterAddedToRoom (PunchConstruct.cs:71-78) spends it as `Creature.SetCurrentHpInternal(Math.Max(1, CurrentHp - StartingHpReduction))` -- CURRENT HP only, MaxHp untouched, and AFTER the Niche max-HP roll that CreateCreature already did
guards.issue: events/punch_off.py:26-28 does `m.max_hp = max(1, m.max_hp - reduction); m.hp = min(m.hp, m.max_hp)` inside create_monsters, i.e. it moves MAX HP and it does so BEFORE the parity pass. Two legs, both EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes_a.py punchhp`): (1) LEGACY -- the two constructs come out at (50, 50) and (49, 49) where the game has max_hp 55 and current HP 55 - NextInt(2,10) (46..53); zero constructs are damaged in the sim, two are in the game. (2) PARITY -- CombatState._assign_parity_monster_hp (combat.py:152-153) runs AFTER create_monsters and assigns `creature.hp = creature.max_hp = hp` (combat.py:242), so both constructs come out at (55, 55) and the reduction is ERASED ENTIRELY. The sim already has the correct slot for this: Monster.adjust_hp_after_added (monsters/base.py:69-77) is the AfterAddedToRoom fix-up that runs after the Niche roll, and PunchConstruct does not implement it. LIVE -- Punch-Off is an ordinary act-2 Underdocks event, both constructs are ported (monsters/underdocks/punch_construct.py), and starting HP is the first thing a combat-parity diff compares.

guards.what: EV-3: BOTH of Punch-Off's draw groups: CalculateVars' NextInt(91, 99) (PunchOff.cs:103), which the sim takes off `self.rng` (events/punch_off.py:61) instead of the per-event base.Rng; AND the encounter's two `base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` reduction draws (PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17, :19), which come off the ENCOUNTER's own Rng in the source but off the shared combat rng in the sim (events/punch_off.py:26 uses create_monsters' `rng` argument, not its `selection_rng` argument, which run.create_combat:1141-1146 seeds with make_encounter_rng -- exactly EncounterModel.base.Rng). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes_a.py punchhp`). The second group is not literally the per-event Rng, but it is the same defect shape and takes EV-3's verdict per rule 3, exactly as the room_full_of_cheese record did for its PlayerRng.Rewards draws rolls on the sim's shared run RNG (`self.rng`) where C# rolls on the per-event `base.Rng`
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-3, one verdict at every site (rule 3). Each C# EventModel gets its own Rng seeded from the run seed + event id, and the sim already models it: Event.__init__ builds `self.event_rng` from make_event_rng(seed, ID) for string-seeded runs (events/base.py:84-88), and 6 modules branch on it. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/event_probes.py eventrng`): 28 of the 34 event modules that roll anything roll ONLY on `self.rng`. LIVE for the parity path that the conformance harness grades -- a shared-rng draw both takes a number the game never takes off that stream and fails to advance the event stream, desyncing the rest of the run. In legacy (RL) mode both are the same random.Random, so the observable is parity-only -- which is an exercised sim mode, not an unreachable one.
